key_insight: GradAudit detects whether a vision-language model likely trained on specific image-text pairs by analyzing internal parameter-gradient patterns that are stable for training samples and noisy for non-training samples.
clinical_relevance: In healthcare AI, this offers a way to audit whether patient images and clinical reports may have been used in model training, supporting privacy, provenance, and copyright safeguards.
method: Compute gradients on candidate image-text pairs rather than relying only on model outputs
Compare gradient stability and alignment between suspected training and non-training examples
Use these gradient signatures to identify genuine cross-modal associations learned during training
evidence_signal: Across medical and general-domain datasets, the method outperformed state-of-the-art baselines for both pretraining and fine-tuning VLLMs, and a copyrighted-content case study showed that prior methods underestimated unauthorized data use.
watch_item: Gradient-based auditing can be computationally intensive and its conclusions still depend on access to model internals and carefully selected reference data.
paper_title: Revealing Training Data Exposure in Vision Language Large Models via Parameter Gradients
